text:
sam: small but weird incident on canary: SSE keepalive chunks arriving out-of-order caused the proxy to split a single logical session into two session ids, and console smoothing made it look like a route switch. impact: duplicate quota attribution across Route-Blue/Route-Green for one tenant.

evelyn: when you say "split" do you mean we saw two different session ids for the same resume token?

sam: yes. timeline in logs (condensed):

```
[09:41:02] proxy-edge: sse open tenant=theta session=aa11 route=blue
[09:41:10] proxy-edge: keepalive chunk seq=14 ts=16432 (arrived)
[09:41:11] proxy-edge: keepalive chunk seq=13 ts=16420 (late/out-of-order)
[09:41:11] proxy-edge: detect-seq-gap -> spawn recovery session=bb22 route=green
[09:41:11] billing: quota charge tenant=theta session=bb22 cost=3
[09:41:12] proxy-edge: original session aa11 resumed/closed
[09:41:12] billing: quota charge tenant=theta session=aa11 cost=3
```

sam: console aggregated per-route smoothing (1m window) then flagged a 200% spike on Route-Green. canary alert fired.

rob: hmm out-of-order chunks should be handled by our chunk-reassembler, not by creating a new session. why did we create bb22? is this a recent change in the reassembler logic?

evelyn: we added an optimization in the proxy to fast-path a late chunk if the reassembly window was closed to reduce latency for normal flows. apparently that fast-path treats a late chunk as a new stream when it crosses a threshold.

sam: consequences: billing double-charged (billing-bot, please confirm) and console rollup misattributed to routes -> noisy canary.

billing-bot: preliminary: two charges for tenant=theta within 2s. mark=potential-duplicate. awaiting ledger reconcile job.

rob: two problems: (1) proxy fast-path causing split sessions, (2) console smoothing + per-route attribution is hiding session lineage so ops see only route-level spikes.

evelyn: quick mitigation ideas:
- increase reassembly window (simple config) to accept late chunks for a short period
- pause the fast-path for canary rollouts touching reassembly code
- in billing: dedupe by resume-token+time-window (like 10s) to avoid double billing on session splits

console-dev: on the console side we can do a fast change: when a route spike is detected, automatically fetch recent session ids/resume tokens for top affected tenants (if available) and show "possible session split" hint with a link to raw traces. low-risk toggle.

rob: do we have telemetry tags emitted when we fast-path a late chunk? we should.

evelyn: not currently. we only emit `chunk_reorder=true` in debug logs. can add a metric `proxy.chunk.reorder.fastpath` with labels route, env, tenant-hash.

sam: rollouts: the canary alarm fired and devs paged. we rolled back the canary at 09:52. but we need a safer rollout plan for chunk reassembly changes.

rob: long-term fixes:
- revert fast-path or make it opt-in per-client capability header
- keep a tiny cross-cluster KV to track resume-token -> last-billed-session for a short TTL to prevent double billing on splits
- enhance console with session lineage UI and raw session fetch on anomalies

sre-oncall: paging note: if this pattern reoccurs, it will generate noisy alerts. propose: temporarily bump the anomaly threshold for route-rate alerts by 3x for the next 1 hour for the canary group to reduce pager noise while we validate fix.

console-dev: can do. also adding a short-term flag `show_session_lineage_on_spike=true` for canary groups.

sam: action items (short):
- evelyn: rollback fast-path (done) and open PR to make reassembly-window configurable (aim 2h)
- rob: billing dedupe rule for resume-token window=10s (wip)
- console-dev: add quick UI hint + toggle for session lineage (aim 4h)
- sre-oncall: bump alert threshold for canary cohort (1h)

evelyn: follow-up RFC for collection: we need to standardize a small set of session lineage fields propagated through the stack (resume-token, origin-proxy, seq-window) and mark those fields as high-priority telemetry so console sampling doesn't drop them during rollouts.

rob: agreed. also add an integration test that simulates out-of-order SSE chunks and asserts no session split and no double-charge.

sam: thanks everyone. tagging @billing-bot and @console-dev for updates. I'll keep the incident thread pinned until the ledger reconcile completes. :white_check_mark:
